title: What a Member Pays on the Restoration of a Ridgecrest Advantage Enrollment
content:
The restored premium balance is what a member must pay on restoration for the coverage months a terminated Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment is brought back for when a good-cause determination restores it.

### The quantities

- **The restored premium balance** is the plan premium for the coverage months restored, together with the arrears collected on restoration, less the relief allowed against it, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end, and it is never less than nothing.
- **The plan premium for the coverage months restored** is the coverage months restored multiplied by the plan premium of a restored coverage month.
- **The coverage months restored** are one, that is 1 coverage month.
- **The plan premium of a restored coverage month** is the monthly plan premium of the plan held taken at the share of it the member meets, rounded to the nearest cent.
- **The share of the monthly plan premium the member meets** is the whole of it, that is 100 per cent of it.
- **The arrears collected on restoration** are the arrears standing when the coverage ended taken at the share of them the plan collects on restoration, rounded to the nearest cent.
- **The arrears standing when the coverage ended** are the plan premium reckoned as owed when the coverage ended less the payments recognised against it, rounded to the nearest cent, and never less than nothing.
- **The share of the arrears the plan collects on restoration** is the whole of them, that is 100 per cent of them.
- **The plan premium reckoned as owed when the coverage ended** is the most recent plan premium charge standing on the premium account.
- **The payments recognised against it** are the most recent plan premium payment standing on the premium account.
- **The relief allowed against it** is nothing.
- **The whole months since the coverage ended** are the whole months that have passed since the coverage end date recorded on the terminated enrollment.

The restoration keeps the original coverage effective date so that the coverage period is continuous again, and reinstatement is granted once for any one terminated enrollment.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a terminated enrollment whose premium account carries a most recent plan premium charge of 225.00 USD and a most recent plan premium payment of 100.00 USD, and a monthly plan premium for the plan held of 75.00 USD.

- Plan premium of a restored coverage month: 75.00 USD taken at the whole of it, so 75.00 USD.
- Plan premium for the coverage months restored: 1 multiplied by 75.00 USD, so 75.00 USD.
- Arrears standing when the coverage ended: 225.00 USD less 100.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent, so 125.00 USD.
- Arrears collected on restoration: 125.00 USD taken at the whole of them, so 125.00 USD.
- Relief allowed against it: nothing.
- Restored premium balance: 75.00 USD together with 125.00 USD, less nothing, rounded once at the end, so **200.00 USD**.
